ap_statistics-m01.stem: A researcher wants to answer the investigative question "Do drivers of electric cars tend to drive more kilometers per week than drivers of gasoline cars?" for the drivers in a city. Which of the following describes the data that the researcher should collect?

options.text: Independent random samples of $36$ drivers of electric cars and $45$ drivers of gasoline cars, with only whether each individual is above or below average recorded.
options.why: Recording only above or below average discards the quantitative variable that the means need.

options.text: Independent random samples of $36$ drivers of electric cars and $45$ drivers of gasoline cars, with the number of kilometers driven in a week recorded for each individual.
options.why: The question compares the mean of a quantitative variable between two groups, so the data needed are independent random samples from the two groups with that variable recorded for every individual.

options.text: One random sample of $81$ drivers in a city, with only the group of each individual recorded.
options.why: The variable that the question compares is not recorded, so the means cannot be compared.

options.text: A random sample of $36$ drivers of electric cars, with the number of kilometers driven in a week recorded for each individual.
options.why: Data from only one of the two groups cannot show a difference between the groups.

ap_statistics-m02.stem: The least-squares line for predicting the cost of the trip (in dollars) from the length of a trip (in miles) has a slope of $0.6$ dollars per mile. The explanatory variable is converted to kilometers (1 mile = 1.609 kilometers) and the least-squares line is found again. What is the slope of the new line?

options.text: About $0.97$ dollars per kilometer.
options.why: Multiplies by the conversion factor instead of dividing by it; a kilometer is a different amount of $x$ than a mile in the opposite way.

options.text: About $0.37$ dollars per kilometer.
options.why: One mile is $1.609$ of a kilometer, so the predicted change per kilometer is $0.6/1.609 \approx 0.37$ dollars.

options.text: About $0.6$ dollars per kilometer.
options.why: The slope is measured per unit of $x$, so it changes when the unit changes from the mile to the kilometer.

options.text: About $-0.37$ dollars per kilometer.
options.why: The sign of the slope does not depend on the units, because the direction of the relationship does not change.

ap_statistics-m03.stem: A least-squares line $\hat y = 30 - 2.2x$ predicts its resale value in thousand dollars from the age of a car in years, using data with $x$ from $2$ to $10$ years and a correlation close to $1$. A researcher considers predictions for $x = 6$, $x = 12$, $x = 22$ and $x = 1$. Which prediction is the most reliable, and why?

options.text: The prediction for $x = 1$, because the correlation is close to $1$.
options.why: $1$ is below the smallest value of $x$ in the data, and a strong correlation within the range does not make predictions outside it reliable.

options.text: The prediction for $x = 6$, because $6$ is between the smallest and the largest values of $x$ in the data.
options.why: The data have values of $x$ from $2$ to $10$, and a prediction inside that range is an interpolation, which is the most reliable kind.

options.text: The prediction for $x = 12$, because it is only a little beyond the largest value of $x$ in the data.
options.why: $12$ is outside the range of the data ($2$ to $10$), so the prediction is an extrapolation, even though it is close to the range.

options.text: The prediction for $x = 22$, because the line is a least-squares line that fits all of the data.
options.why: A good fit within the range of the data does not show that the line continues to hold far outside the range.
